channel.title: Merkle Street
channel.description: Merkle Street reports crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, layer 2s, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and protocol upgrades.

item.title: Destination Coin or Output Token: What Unsticks a Swap?
item.description: A stuck cross-chain swap can mean a pending deposit, an unfinished route or a delayed payout; check the stage before changing the destination or retrying.

item.title: Three Pool Checks Before a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: Compare the pools on your route, estimate price impact and fees, then check whether the quoted price can hold while each chain confirms the swap.

item.title: Destination Execution Failure After Bridging Explained
item.description: A destination execution failure means the bridge transfer and the action after it had different outcomes. Your source-chain transaction may have…

item.title: What a wallet timeout means during a cross-chain swap
item.description: A wallet timeout usually ends the signing session, not the swap; check the source-chain transaction and destination status before signing again or closing the route.

item.title: Five Steps to Consolidate Small Layer-Two Balances
item.description: A practical sequence for checking small layer-two balances, choosing one destination, comparing bridge costs, and moving tokens without letting fees consume their value.

item.title: Why a Mantle Bridge Swap Can Pay Out Less Than Its Quote
item.description: A Mantle bridge swap quote is an estimate across several steps; market movement, route fees and the difference between expected and minimum output affect what arrives.

item.title: What to Do When a Team Transfer Uses an Unsupported Token
item.description: A team transfer can confirm on-chain even when the receiving service cannot credit the token; identify the network, preserve proof, then use the right recovery path.

item.title: Why Crypto Bridge Transfers Take Time
item.description: Bridge wait times depend on source-chain finality, bridge design and destination processing; tracking each step helps distinguish normal delay from a stuck transfer.

item.title: How Mantle Integrators Can Guard Against Wrong-Chain Deposits
item.description: Wrong-chain deposits reach an address on the wrong network, so Mantle integrators need chain-aware instructions, event checks and a clear recovery path.

item.title: How to Check Which Token Arrives After a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A cross-chain swap can pass through several contracts, so check the destination network, token contract and completed output before treating the quote as what arrived.

item.title: Move Collateral Before Opening a Cross-Chain Position
item.description: Moving collateral across chains means planning the transfer, bridge, destination deposit and position entry as separate steps, with timing and margin risk in view.

item.title: Why a Swapped Token May Need Manual Import
item.description: A cross-chain swap can finish while the destination wallet hides the received token; manual import adds its verified address to the wallet’s display, not the chain.

item.title: Why Ethereum Is the Source Chain for Mantle Bridge Deposits
item.description: For a canonical Mantle transfer, Ethereum is the source chain; choose it when the asset, settlement path, timing and fee budget fit your business controls.

item.title: Mantle Bridge: Check Which Token Will Arrive
item.description: A bridge can move an asset across networks or route it through a swap. Check the destination token and contract before signing, because a ticker alone does not identify what arrives.

item.title: How wrapped bitcoin works on Ethereum
item.description: Wrapped bitcoin gives BTC an ERC-20 form on Ethereum, backed by reserves but dependent on an issuer, a redemption route and market demand to hold its price near BTC.

item.title: Starknet opens vote on studying an independent post-quantum chain
item.description: Starknet opened a seven-day, nonbinding STRK poll on researching an independent post-quantum Layer 1, a first step that would not approve leaving Ethereum.

item.title: Why Treasury Must Compare Net Value Before Bridging
item.description: Treasury should compare what arrives after bridge fees, swaps, slippage and destination costs, because the amount sent is not the amount available to use.

item.title: Why Bitcoin Becomes a Token on Another Chain
item.description: Wrapped Bitcoin works with another chain’s apps because a bridge holds BTC and issues a matching token, whose redemption depends on the bridge working.

item.title: How to Swap Into Collateral for a Remote Lending Market
item.description: To use a remote lending market, move an accepted asset to its chain, swap if needed, then supply it to the market contract before borrowing against it.

item.title: Why a BSC-to-Arbitrum Swap Needs Gas on Both Chains
item.description: A BSC-to-Arbitrum stablecoin transfer can stall before or after the swap if gas is missing: keep BNB for BSC and ETH for Arbitrum, and verify the route.
